$comment: What the public site must never do (the quality bar of work order 3, lane C): no tracking, no cookies, no request to another origin. scripts/check-no-tracking.mjs holds the built public output to it on every pull request (Checks, 'Public site checks'). The site's own address, once the user sets it in config/site.json, is the only other address a page may name outside a link. A link a visitor chooses to follow (an <a> or an <area>) is not a request and is not checked.

storage.reason: Two things a visitor chooses are kept in their browser's localStorage: their own saved questions and canvases (src/lib/saved.ts), and their choice of the light or dark theme, one word under one key (src/lib/themeChoice.ts, read by a short script in every page's head so the page is drawn in the theme chosen). Each is read and written by the page on the visitor's own device and is never sent anywhere: the page makes no request that carries it. Neither is a cookie, which every request would send to the server. Nothing else may keep anything on the visitor's device.

$tracker_signatures_comment: Analytics and tag products named by the address they load from or the call they make, so that an ordinary word (a plausible value, a double click) does not match. A product not listed is still caught where it matters: by the rule that a page or a script may not name another origin.

$forbidden_files_comment: Server code Cloudflare Pages would run for a visitor's request. The site is static files only; one that runs code could set a cookie or call another origin.
$forbidden_env_comment: Set at build time, PUBLIC_QUERY_SERVICE (src/lib/data.ts) sends every question to that address, which would be another origin. It must be empty in the build that is checked and deployed.
